comparison: Perfect agreement on model validation (C89, C90). Both accept the computational model quality metrics, predictive accuracies, and parameter recovery correlations as adequate validation despite lower individual model recovery.

Strong agreement on differential brain development trajectories (C7, C94-C98). Both accept the LCS model findings showing hippocampal volume increases while striatal volume remains stable, with no concerns raised about the statistical approach.

Strong agreement on striatal findings (C10, C100-C102, C141-C142). Both explicitly accept that striatal volume was associated with both learning conditions, contrasting with adult patterns. Peer reviewers acknowledge this lack of specificity as a valid developmental finding.

Strong agreement on selective hippocampal-delayed learning association (C8, C104, C106, C133). Both evaluations endorse this as a key finding with adequate statistical support from four-variate LCS modeling. Peer reviewers call it 'the key contribution.'

Strong agreement on less differentiated memory systems in children (C11, C12, C109, C144, C153, C165). Both accept the interpretation that children show reduced neural specificity compared to adults. Editor explicitly endorses 'neurally less differentiated and more cooperative memory systems.'

Agreement on simulation-based optimal parameters (C85, C86, C87). Both accept the approach of comparing children's parameters to simulated optimal values. OpenEval emphasizes longitudinal improvement toward optimal values; peer reviewers praise the computational modeling approach without criticism.

Agreement on feedback timing effects through reaction time and inverse temperature (C3, C4, C83, C84). Both accept these correlational findings. OpenEval provides detailed statistical support; peer reviewers accept without questioning the behavioral and modeling results.

Agreement on longitudinal behavioral improvements (C115-C117). Both accept win-stay increases and lose-shift decreases. OpenEval notes consistency with prior literature; peer reviewers explicitly affirm improvements in reinforcement learning over the 2-year period.

Agreement on longitudinal improvements and developmental implications (C179, C180). Both accept the 2-year improvements in learning parameters. OpenEval notes the inference about dynamic developmental period is reasonable; peer reviewers explicitly endorse children 'improve towards more optimal value-based decision-making strategies.'

Divergent evaluation of sex differences (C118). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to potential confounding and inconsistent prior literature, recommending cautious interpretation. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED without explicit discussion, though lack of criticism may reflect implicit acceptance of authors' own cautious framing.

Agreement on correlation patterns between reaction time and inverse temperature (C76, C77). OpenEval includes these in broader feedback timing analysis; peer reviewers specifically praise data visualization showing these correlational details without questioning the patterns.

Divergent evaluation of episodic memory findings (C134). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to inconsistent results across datasets and lack of direct testing of poor learner speculation. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED, acknowledging hippocampal association with delayed learning without raising concerns about the episodic memory null result.

Partial overlap on hippocampal interpretation (C135, C136). OpenEval rates interpretation as SUPPORTED when contextualized with aging research. Peer reviewers accept the hippocampal findings broadly but don't explicitly discuss the aging comparison or episodic memory aspects.

Divergent evaluation of feedback timing mechanism (C154-C156). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of functional brain measures to test decision-making vs. value update mechanisms. Peer reviewers SUPPORTED the feedback timing effects without questioning the proposed mechanism or noting the absence of functional data.

Peer reviewers explicitly accept brain-behavior correlation stability (C110, C111) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval does not have a separate result for this finding, though these claims appear in R4 context where longitudinal stability strengthens the hippocampal-delayed learning association.

OpenEval provides detailed SUPPORTED evaluation of discussion contextualizing findings with adult literature and methodological factors (C121-C132). No corresponding peer review result explicitly evaluates these interpretive claims, though peer reviewers generally praise the computational approach.

OpenEval rates practical implications and future applications (C166-C175) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are speculative extensions beyond what data directly support. No corresponding peer review evaluation addresses these forward-looking claims.

OpenEval evaluates sensitivity analyses with/without poor learners (C176-C178) as SUPPORTED for demonstrating sample sensitivity, though interpretation is speculative. No corresponding peer review result explicitly addresses these sensitivity analyses.
